task: Purge follow-up: dangling references to the retired evidence tree + the skills re-pin

anchor.note: Owned by the captain after the t33 takeover; the commit that carries this file is the change itself.

finding: The purge removed the retired evidence tree but four LIVE reference sites still named it by path, so the repository carried dead pointers to content that no longer exists.

sitesFixed.was: the BRAND_ALLOWLIST comment pointed at a follow-up note inside the deleted tree
sitesFixed.now: points at the per-entry reasons declared in the same file

sitesFixed.was: the guard's failure message told the reader to consult the deleted note
sitesFixed.now: tells the reader to consult the X1 allowlist declared in this file

sitesFixed.was: the header comment carried the deleted prototype's full path
sitesFixed.now: describes the worked example as a scratch prototype not carried here

sitesFixed.was: the case-table provenance cell named the retired phase

vendorLock.rule: skills/** has ONE writer per wave and the re-pin must land in the SAME commit (§9/§11)
vendorLock.mechanism: computed with the gate's own algorithm (sorted repo-relative paths, per-file sha256 over LF-normalized bytes, then sha256 of "<path>\n<sha>\n" lines); written by a targeted replacement of the single old digest so the file's formatting is untouched, because a JSON round-trip was byte-different and a full re-serialize would have produced a spurious diff

identifierScanAfterChange.tracked: 0 real hits; the single raw match is the exempt third-party platform brand ("macOS Apple Silicon", a Rust target-triple note)
identifierScanAfterChange.buildOutputs: 0 hits beyond the same exempt line
identifierScanAfterChange.falseAlarmRecorded: The captain first flagged this change's own evidence prose as a violation. Re-measured precisely: the only matches were the SUBSTRING inside the exempt platform brand, never the retired project identifier. Recorded because a substring scan cannot distinguish the two and the next reader should not repeat the alarm.
